extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline personnel, and attorneys subject to USPTO discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedural requirements governing approval of an affidavit of resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27, grounds for practitioner misconduct under the USPTO Rules of Professional Conduct, publication and reinstatement consequences following exclusion on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit of Resignation under 37 C.F.R. § 11.27
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavit of Resignation submitted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.27 for the purpose of being excluded on consent; must comply with the requirements of § 11.27(a)/(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged that his consent is freely and voluntarily rendered, he is aware of the pending disciplinary complaint, understands the legal and factual consequences of consenting to exclusion, and consents to being excluded from practice before the USPTO in patent, trademark, and other non-patent matters. The Director may approve the affidavit and exclude the practitioner on consent.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32 — Director's authority
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO Director has authority to approve an Affidavit of Resignation and to exclude a practitioner on consent from practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval and exclusion are taken pursuant to these statutory provisions in conjunction with 37 C.F.R. § 11.27.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.102(a) — Abide by client's decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to abide by a client's decisions concerning the objectives of representation and, as required by § 11.104, to fail to consult with the client as to the means by which the client's objectives are to be pursued, and to fail to abide by a client's decision in a matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations included failing to follow a client's instructions regarding prosecution and foreign filings and failing to keep the client informed of abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.103 — Reasonable diligence and promptness
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to act with reasonable diligence and promptness in representing a client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples alleged: not filing a response to an office action before its due date, not filing promised continuation-in-part, and not responding to a Final Rejection leading to abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(2) — Reasonable consultation with client
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to reasonably consult with the client about the means by which the client's objectives are to be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failures included not consulting the client about prosecution steps and not communicating about revival or subsequent office actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(3) — Keep client reasonably informed
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to keep the client reasonably informed about the status of the matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations: Respondent did not inform the client about application abandonments, revival, or Final Rejection status.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(a)(4) — Promptly comply with requests for information
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to promptly comply with reasonable requests for information from the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failure to provide timely information about filings, revivals, and status updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.104(b) — Explain sufficiently for informed decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to explain a matter to the extent reasonably necessary to permit the client to make informed decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged deficiencies in communications about prosecution strategy and the consequences of office actions and abandonments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(d) — Prompt delivery of client funds/property
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to promptly deliver to the client or a third person any funds or other property that the client or third person is entitled to receive, upon request by the client or third person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegation: disagreement about whether Respondent was holding client funds to pay a foreign renewal fee and whether those funds were delivered or used as instructed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.115(f)(3) — Trust account recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to keep readily accessible to the practitioner receipt and disbursement journals containing a record of deposits to and withdrawals from client trust accounts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failures to maintain or provide accounting records that frustrated the OED investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.116(a)(2) — Withdrawal for impairment
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to withdraw from the representation when the practitioner's physical or mental condition materially impairs the ability of the practitioner to represent the client.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cited as a potential rule implicated by the conduct; no specific medical facts recited in the order.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(a) — False statements in disciplinary matters
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to knowingly make false statements of material fact in connection with a disciplinary matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent was alleged to have made false statements to the client about filing actions and about the status of the application; false statements in disciplinary contexts are separately proscribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.801(b) — Failure to cooperate with OED
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to fail to cooperate with the Office of Enrollment and Discipline in an investigation of any matter before it, or to knowingly fail to respond to a lawful demand or request for information from an admissions or disciplinary authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alleged failure to provide complete or timely responses and accounting records to OED's Request for Information, frustrating the investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(c) — Dishonesty, fraud, deceit, misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to engage in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allegations included telling the client that Respondent had pointed out an examiner's error and was awaiting a response when no response had been filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d) — Conduct prejudicial to administration of justice
rubrics_metrics.description: It is professional misconduct to engage in conduct that is prejudicial to the administration of justice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad proscriptions cited by the OED Director as implicated by the alleged pattern of conduct in client representation and interactions with OED.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to provide complete and timely responses to OED inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Practitioners must provide complete and timely responses and accounting records to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline during investigations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record alleges that Respondent's failure to provide complete and correct responses and accounting records frustrated OED's investigation — failure to cooperate is actionable under § 11.801(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences for reinstatement under 37 C.F.R. § 11.60
rubrics_metrics.description: If and when the excluded practitioner applies for reinstatement under § 11.60, the OED Director will conclusively presume, for purposes of determining the application for reinstatement, that the allegations in the disciplinary complaint are true and that the practitioner could not have successfully defended himself against those allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent acknowledged this presumption in his affidavit; compliance with § 11.60 is required upon any request for reinstatement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 after exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall comply fully with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly requires compliance with § 11.58; the order does not restate § 11.58's text but mandates adherence as a condition of exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Final Order and Official Gazette notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at the OED FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The notice must summarize the exclusion on consent, the nature of the pending complaint and allegations, and the regulatory bases for the action; disciplinary decisions are posted for public reading at the OED Reading Room.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit acknowledgments required in this case (specific attestations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent's affidavit included specific acknowledgments: consent freely and voluntarily rendered; awareness of pending complaint and alleged violations; recognition that OED will presume allegations true for reinstatement; having read and understood relevant rules (§§ 11.5(b), 11.27, 11.58, 11.59, and 11.60); and consent to exclusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order summarizes these affirmations as part of the affidavit approval process; such acknowledgments bear on the validity of a consent exclusion.
